recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say what comes out as a common factor and what is left inside the limit.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Take e³ out as a common factor
steps.margin_note: First mark. e³ is a fixed number, not a function of x, so it comes outside the limit sign. What is left inside is the plain standard form (eˣ − 1)/x.
steps.memory_tip: e^(x+3) is e³ times eˣ. Split the power at the plus sign and the constant part comes straight out.
lines: Putting x = 0 gives 0/0, so the numerator is rewritten first.
e^(x+3) = eˣ · e³, so  e^(x+3) − e³ = e³(eˣ − 1)
e³ is a constant, so it comes outside the limit:

recall.must_convey: That e^(x+3) = eˣ · e³, so the numerator is e³(eˣ − 1) and the constant e³ comes outside the limit.
accept: e power x plus three is e power x times e cubed
take e cubed out as a common factor
e cubed is a constant so it comes outside the limit
e cube ni common ga bayataki teeyali
the numerator becomes e cubed into e power x minus one

steps.why: The law e^(a+b) = eᵃ · eᵇ separates the fixed part of the power from the part that moves. e³ carries no x, so it plays no role in the limit and is taken outside, leaving the standard form behind.
common_mistakes: Treating e³ as part of the limit and letting it change as x → 0.
Writing e^(x+3) = eˣ + e³, adding the powers instead of multiplying.

steps.label: Apply (eˣ − 1)/x → 1
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The limit inside is exactly the standard one and equals 1, so the constant already outside is the whole answer. Leave it as e³; do not turn it into a decimal.
steps.memory_tip: The limit inside is worth 1, so the answer is whatever was carried outside.

recall.must_convey: That the standard limit equals 1, so the value is e³.
accept: the standard limit is one so the answer is e cubed
e power x minus one over x is one
one times e cubed is e cubed

steps.why: Quoting the standard limit is what earns the mark. e³ is an exact value, so writing 20.09 instead loses the exact form the board expects.
common_mistakes: Replacing e³ by a decimal such as 20.09.
Cancelling e³ against something and giving the answer as 1.
